$comment: Ratchet baseline for forked sibling pages. A route that exists under two or more league directories in src/pages/ is a SIBLING; a sibling whose largest copy exceeds `thinPageMaxLines` is FORKED — a page built twice instead of a component built once. This list may only SHRINK. tests/page-fork-ratchet.test.ts fails if a route is added (a new fork shipped) and also fails if a listed route becomes thin or disappears (so the baseline is retightened rather than quietly leaving slack). To unify a route, extract its body into a shared page component, reduce each league's route to a thin wrapper, then delete its entry here.

notes.threshold: 80 is not arbitrary. At the time of recording the largest thin sibling was pecking-order/[year]/[week].astro at 75 lines and the smallest forked one was mock-draft/[sessionId].astro at 98, so the cut falls in an empty band rather than through the middle of a distribution. Raising it to slip a page through is a change to this file and will show up in review.
notes.scale: These 24 routes carry ~53,100 lines between them. rosters.astro alone is 12,521 + 2,465 + 245; players.astro is 4,246 + 2,249; playoffs.astro is 2,275 + 2,939.
notes.bestFirstTarget: DONE (2026-09-01). lineup.astro was the purest fork in the repo — 2,573 and 2,579 lines differing in twelve places — and is now one shared component (src/components/shared/lineup/LineupPage.astro) behind two ~60-line route wrappers. Next cheapest by the same measure: playoffs.astro (2,275 vs 2,939) and players.astro (4,246 vs 2,249).
notes.knownGap: Size is measured on the ROUTE FILE only. A pair of thin routes delegating to two per-league component trees would pass this guard while being just as forked. That hole is real; it is accepted because the regression this exists to stop is the cheap one — copying a league's page file to the next league and editing it — and because measuring duplication across component trees needs a different tool than a line count.
notes.whyNotRatchetLines: The metric is the SET of forked routes, not their line count. Ratcheting total lines would fail this test on any ordinary three-line bugfix to rosters.astro, which is hostile and would get the guard disabled. What must not regress is the NUMBER OF PAGES built twice.
notes.draftBroadcast: draft-broadcast.astro (theleague:225, afl-fantasy:212) landed on main in PRs #650-#653 while the branch introducing this guard was in flight, so it is baselined rather than fixed here. It is NOT unavoidable and should not be read as blessed: both copies already share the same island (components/shared/draft-broadcast/DraftBroadcast), so what is forked is only the per-league server-side data assembly, and their own header documents the whole difference as two things — TheLeague drafts as one unit where the AFL drafts by conference, and TheLeague's board is rookies-only. That is a tractable unification and a good Tier-2 target; it was kept out of a Storybook PR because turning it into a draft-broadcast refactor is how a reviewable change stops being reviewable.
